It controls how input sections from object files are arranged into memory and defines symbols/addresses.
Sets the ELF executable entry point; Cortex-M reset normally uses the
is removed, will Cortex-M fail to boot?
Not necessarily. CPU normally gets SP/PC from the vector table.
Defines available memory regions, origin, size, and attributes.
Places section's runtime/VMA address in RAM.
Stores the section's load image in Flash while its runtime address is in RAM.
Address where section exists/runs at runtime.
Address where initial section contents are stored in the image.
Initial values must persist in Flash but variables must run from writable RAM.
get copied from Flash to RAM?
No. It depends on the section currently being placed.
It only needs to become zero in RAM; storing zeros in Flash is unnecessary.
Reserves memory for the section without requiring a normal load image.
Read-only constants, strings, lookup tables, etc.
It doesn't need runtime writes, so nonvolatile Flash is suitable.
Prevents vector table from being garbage-collected.
input sections from all object files.
Removes unwanted input sections from the final image.
Cortex-M uses a descending stack; the initial SP starts at the top of RAM.
technically one byte beyond the last RAM byte?
It represents the top/boundary of the stack region; the first push decrements SP into valid RAM.
